_comment: Example MCP server configuration for BlackEclipse. Copy to `mcp-servers.json`
(same folder) — that file is gitignored because it may hold scoped env values.
Transports: `stdio` (a local subprocess via npx/python), `http` (remote
Streamable-HTTP) and `sse` (remote SSE). `secret_refs` maps an env var the
server reads to a NAMED secret stored encrypted in the vault (Settings > MCP
Servers > Secret vault); a remote server uses `auth` (kind/name/prefix/secretRef)
instead. Never put a raw API key in this file. `enabled` defaults to false and
`selected_tools` to empty: nothing activates until you choose it. `selected_tools`
may be an exact list OR `{include, exclude}` with globs (include wins; an empty
include selects nothing). `tool_effects` declares a tool's real effect (read is
the only one that needs no per-call approval); `trust: "untrusted"` requires
approval for every non-read call and forbids annotation-sourced activation.
`data_source_tools` declares a selected read tool as a NATIVE retrieval source
(tool -> dataType) so native source planning can consider it; an undeclared tool
stays directly callable and is still never Eclipse-verified. `lazy` registers
tool declarations from an on-disk cache and connects on the first call.
`tools: {resources|prompts}` registers those utility tools only when the live
server advertises the capability. `keepalive_interval`/`idle_timeout_seconds`/
`max_lifetime_seconds` tune the connection lifetime. `ssl_verify` accepts true,
false, or a CA-bundle path; `client_cert`/`client_key` enable mTLS (a combined
PEM, or [cert,key], or [cert,key,passphrase]). `resource_schemes` narrows which
resource URI schemes this server may read (the global allowlist is a hard
ceiling; narrowing can only remove schemes). Values support
`${VAR}`/`${env:VAR}` and `${workspaceFolder}`/`${userHome}`/`${pathSeparator}`
(a remote url/auth with an unresolved variable is refused, never sent literally).
Remote endpoints must be https and are refused if they resolve to a private
address (loopback http is allowed for local testing). `live_supply_chain_check`
(default true) queries the public OSV advisory API for the package an `npx`/
`uvx` server is about to launch: a confirmed malware advisory refuses the spawn,
a network failure allows it and is labelled. It runs at the spawn path only —
never in Test, never at boot for a `lazy` server, never for a non-package
command. Set it to false to skip the (8s-timeout) outbound check entirely.

servers.name: Local files
servers.description: Read files under the app folder. Uses an include/exclude filter and narrows resource reads to file://.

servers.name: Word / Excel / PowerPoint (Office)
servers.description: Creates local Office files. Marked untrusted so every write needs an explicit per-call approval.

servers.name: Notion (local token)
servers.description: Official Notion server, run locally with an integration token. Lazy-started from cache; needs the vault secret 'notion_integration_token'. (The hosted OAuth Notion server is a separate preset, 'notion_remote'.)

servers.name: Google Sheets
servers.description: Community Google Sheets server (service-account or OAuth JSON). Store the credential FILE PATH as a vault secret.

servers.name: Excel files
servers.description: Reads/writes local .xlsx workbooks (read tools need no approval; write tools do).

servers.name: Tavily web search
servers.description: Web search + page extraction. `tavily-search` is declared a native web_research data source (still external, never Eclipse-verified).

servers.name: Brave Search
servers.description: Second independent search provider (news, filings context).

servers.name: Yahoo Finance
servers.description: Quotes/history/news. Kept-alive every 60s. Treat as EXTERNAL and unverified.

servers.name: Knowledge-graph memory
servers.description: A local knowledge graph. Resource/prompt utility tools are registered only if the server advertises them.

servers.name: Twelve Data (remote OAuth)
servers.description: Remote OAuth 2.1 server. No vault secret is stored; use Sign in on the server card and complete the device flow.

servers.name: Remote MCP (HTTP)
servers.description: Template for a remote Streamable-HTTP server: vault-backed bearer token, a custom CA bundle, mTLS client cert/key, and idle/lifetime recycling. Remote endpoints must be https; private hosts are refused.
